experiment: Random Mask Ablation: CA Signal Validation
description: Compare FCBoost CA-derived masks against random static masks to validate whether CA selection provides meaningful signal beyond any static boost.

config.mask_structure: F=8 RoPE pairs per KV head (16 boosted channels out of 128)
config.quantization: K=INT2, V=INT2, boosted channels=INT4, sink=32, buffer=128

fcboost_ca_mask.description: FCBoost v2 with CA-derived mask (3-seed average from main experiment)

question_1.question: Does the random mask improve over KIVI-KV2* (no boost)?
question_1.answer: No. Random mask average (64.44%) is actually slightly below KIVI-KV2* (66.11%), a difference of -1.67pp. Random boosting of arbitrary channels does not reliably help and may even hurt slightly, suggesting that boosting wrong channels can introduce noise.

question_2.question: Does FCBoost (CA mask) significantly outperform the random mask mean?
question_2.answer: Yes. FCBoost CA mask (71.11%) outperforms random mask mean (64.44%) by +6.67pp. This is a substantial gap, demonstrating that the CA-derived channel selection provides genuinely useful information about quantization sensitivity. The CA signal identifies channels where precision matters most, rather than randomly distributing the precision budget.

analysis.conclusion: The CA-derived mask provides a meaningful signal beyond simply applying any static boost. Random masks perform comparably to (or slightly worse than) no boost at all, while the CA mask achieves +6.67pp over random masks and +5.00pp over the no-boost baseline. This validates that the Contextual Agreement metric correctly identifies quantization-sensitive RoPE frequency channels.
